knowledge:
- key_parameters: subset.row=Specifies a subset of genes (e.g., highly variable genes) on which to perform the correction to mitigate noise ;; correct.all=Logical indicating whether corrected values should be returned for all genes by extrapolating from the subset used for correction ;; restrict=A list of cell indices specifying a restricted subset of cells in each batch (e.g., controls) to compute the correction, which is then extrapolated to all other cells ;; PARAM=A BatchelorParam subclass object (e.g., FastMnnParam(), ClassicMnnParam(), RescaleParam()) passed to batchCorrect() or correctExperiments() to dispatch to a specific correction method ;; batch=A vector specifying the batch of origin for each cell when a single combined object is supplied instead of multiple separate batch objects
- alternatives: limma::removeBatchEffect=Designed for bulk genomics data and requires explicit knowledge of other factors of variation, whereas batchelor does not ;; fastMNN() vs mnnCorrect()=fastMNN() performs correction in a low-dimensional PCA space and is much faster and better suited for scRNA-seq, whereas mnnCorrect() operates in gene expression space and is slower but more robust to certain violations of orthogonality assumptions ;; clusterMNN() vs fastMNN()=clusterMNN() is a more conservative strategy that preserves separation between pre-defined clusters across batches but does not adjust for intra-cluster structure differences ;; rescaleBatches() vs regressBatches()=rescaleBatches() centers batches in log-expression space and preserves sparsity by downscaling counts, whereas regressBatches() performs linear regression using ResidualMatrix which does not preserve sparsity but avoids dense matrix creation
- when_to_use: Use when combining single-cell RNA-seq datasets from different batches, times, or laboratories to remove batch effects for downstream exploratory analyses (like clustering and visualization) without requiring prior knowledge of cell-type composition.
- pitfalls: Do not use corrected expression values directly for downstream differential expression (DE) analyses, as batch correction can introduce artifacts; instead, use a blocking factor in DE models ;; rescaleBatches() assumes that the population composition of each batch is identical, making it unsuitable for biological replicates with varying cell-type compositions (best reserved for technical replicates) ;; fastMNN() and multiBatchPCA() use stochastic PCA methods (IRLBA) by default, so set.seed() must be called beforehand to ensure reproducible results

workflows.name: fast_mnn_correction
workflows.intent: Correct batch effects in single-cell RNA-seq datasets using the fast Mutual Nearest Neighbors (MNN) method in PCA space.
workflows.stages: 1. Perform quality control on cells ;; 2. Subset datasets to common genes ;; 3. Normalize sequencing depth across batches using multiBatchNorm ;; 4. Model gene variance and select highly variable genes (HVGs) ;; 5. Run fastMNN to obtain corrected low-dimensional coordinates
workflows.code:
library(scRNAseq)
sce1 <- ZeiselBrainData()
sce2 <- TasicBrainData()

library(scuttle)
sce1 <- addPerCellQC(sce1, subsets=list(Mito=grep("mt-", rownames(sce1))))
qc1 <- quickPerCellQC(colData(sce1), sub.fields="subsets_Mito_percent")
sce1 <- sce1[,!qc1$discard]

sce2 <- addPerCellQC(sce2, subsets=list(Mito=grep("mt_", rownames(sce2))))
qc2 <- quickPerCellQC(colData(sce2), sub.fields="subsets_Mito_percent")
sce2 <- sce2[,!qc2$discard]

universe <- intersect(rownames(sce1), rownames(sce2))
sce1 <- sce1[universe,]
sce2 <- sce2[universe,]

out <- multiBatchNorm(sce1, sce2)
sce1 <- out[[1]]
sce2 <- out[[2]]

library(scran)
dec1 <- modelGeneVar(sce1)
dec2 <- modelGeneVar(sce2)
combined.dec <- combineVar(dec1, dec2)
chosen.hvgs <- getTopHVGs(combined.dec, n=5000)

library(batchelor)
set.seed(101)
f.out <- fastMNN(A=sce1, B=sce2, subset.row=chosen.hvgs)

workflows.name: cluster_mnn_correction
workflows.intent: Merge batches conservatively by matching pre-defined cluster labels across different datasets.
input: sce1 (SingleCellExperiment of batch 1 with cluster annotations)
sce2 (SingleCellExperiment of batch 2 with cluster annotations)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter out unclassified cells ;; 2. Run clusterMNN using pre-defined cluster labels to identify meta-clusters across batches
workflows.code:
not.unclass <- sce2$broad_type!="Unclassified"
clust.out <- clusterMNN(sce1, sce2[,not.unclass],
    subset.row=chosen.hvgs,
    clusters=list(sce1$level1class, sce2$broad_type[not.unclass])) 

clust.info <- metadata(clust.out)$cluster
split(clust.info$cluster, clust.info$meta)

workflows.name: batch_rescaling
workflows.intent: Center batches in log-expression space on a per-gene basis while preserving sparsity (best for technical replicates).
workflows.stages: 1. Run rescaleBatches to obtain a corrected expression matrix wrapped in a SingleCellExperiment
